messages:
maria: Quick design pass attached — noticed a few confusing bits in the playground streaming UI: stop vs pause language, token counter density, and how the prompt library peek interacts with live stream. prototype: https://figma.com/proto/playground-stream-density
sam: Nice — can you highlight the top 2 UX regressions we should fix before the beta sweep?
alex: From implementation POV the main pain is `Stop` triggering a full interrupt vs `Pause` yielding a soft freeze. Right now both use the same affordance which makes expectations unclear. I can wire separate actions but need copy and a tiny state machine.
maria: Top two: 1) label clarity for interrupt controls (users expect immediate cancel on Stop, but regen uses Pause semantics), 2) token counter placement — it's too noisy in the message rail during streaming and steals attention from the stream progress.
aria: Accessibility nit: the streaming output area needs `aria-live="polite"` and we should ensure the token counter is not an extra noisy live region. Also the Stop button needs a programmatic name that describes action (e.g., "Stop generation and discard partial" vs "Pause generation").
sam: Good call on aria-live. For copy, what about: primary button = "Stop and cancel" (red), secondary = "Pause" (neutral)?
maria: I prefer shorter: primary = "Stop" with tooltip "Stops and discards current generation"; secondary = "Pause" tooltip "Pause output, can resume" — tooltips for discoverability but persistent labels kept short.
alex: Implementation detail: if Stop is destructive we should prompt on >5s generated content? Mobile will struggle with modals. Maybe toast that says "Partial generation discarded" with undo for 5s.
aria: Undo toast is better than modal for accessibility. Also ensure focus management: if screenreader user hits Stop, focus should move to the toast with the undo button.
maria: Token counter: two proposals — inline compact count below the prompt (low density) or floating pill in top-right of stream (high visibility). Thoughts?
sam: Lean low density for new users, but provide a toggle in settings (show token pill) for power users.
alex: Technically easy to add toggle. Also suggest we debounce the counter updates to 1s so the render doesn't clog main thread during heavy streams.
aria: Also ensure color contrast for the pill meets AA when shown over the stream. Current blue-on-white mock fails for 14px text.
maria: Prompt library peek: when open it currently scrolls the active conversation out of view during streaming. Suggest split panel overlay so stream remains visible and stream controls remain accessible.
alex: Split panel is fine but complicates responsive. I can do overlay on small screens, split on wide screens.
sam: Can we ship a A/B: overlay vs split for 2 weeks to see metrics on interaction with tokens/regenerate?
maria: Yes — let's spec A/B with these metrics: regenerate usage, stop vs pause ratio, token counter toggles, and prompt library open rate.
aria: Accessibility test items: keyboard nav to stop/pause, proper aria labels on undo toast, screenreader flow when prompt library opens (announce that stream continues), and contrast checks for token pill.
edev: deploy-bot: Drafted a small experiment branch `playground/stream-ux-toggles` with initial copy changes and aria attributes. CI passing.
maria: Sweet — I'll update the figma with the toast and tooltips, add copy variants for the A/B, and add the accessibility checklist. Assigning follow-ups: @alex for implement toggles + debounce, @aria for a11y test plan, @sam for metric spec.
sam: I'll set up the dashboard slices and events. ETA next week for rollout readiness. :thumbsup:
alex: I'll queue the PR and include screenshots for mobile.
aria: I'll run axe+NVDA tests once the branch is up.
maria: Thanks team — small scope, big clarity wins. :sparkles:
